summary: Hear Earth(The Earth Information Jukebox) is an open web app that turns real NASA Earth data into sound, so blind and low-vision people can explore it by ear, not just see it. Users choose a topic: global temperature (NASA GISS GISTEMP), sea-ice extent (NSIDC), or ocean temperature imagery (NASA GIBS). The app then generates a soundscape live in the browser. Numeric data drive pitch, chord layers and pulses on a musical pentatonic scale. NASA images are cut into 28 vertical bands, and their brightness, warmth, hue, saturation and contrast become pitch, timbre, harmony and rhythm. Every chart has a text summary and a data table, and the app works by keyboard and screen reader. It is available in English, Arabic and French. A voice agent answers questions out loud, using only verified data. We label image-derived sound clearly, never invent values, and keep projections separate from observations. EarthVibe makes Earth science accessible, engaging and multi-sensory.
details: What it does. Hear Earth pairs NASA Earth data with sound generated live in the browser (Web Audio API). It has two paths. In the numeric path, the monthly global temperature anomaly (GISTEMP v4, vs 1951–1980) sets the pitch (warmer is higher) and its rate of change sets the pulse count. Sea-ice extent from the NSIDC Sea Ice Index sets the number of chord layers and the brightness. In the image path, a NASA GIBS image is resized, split into 28 vertical bands and scanned left to right. Brightness sets pitch, warmth sets timbre, hue adds a second harmony note, saturation sets its strength, and contrast sets the pulse count. All notes come from a pentatonic scale so the result is musical, and loudness is never used for data
